1.title: A shepherd, not a courtier
1.text: Amos was 'among the herdmen of Tekoa' — a working man from the Judean hills, not a court prophet. His words are dated 'two years before the earthquake,' a quake still remembered generations later.

1.template: But I will send a fire into the house of {0}

1.question: In Amos 1:9, why is judgment pronounced against Tyre?
options: They delivered up the whole captivity to Edom, and remembered not the brotherly covenant
They broke the covenant of peace and sold their own people to foreign enemies
They waged war against their kinsmen and destroyed the cities of Israel without mercy
They offered sacrifices to the idols of Baal upon the high mountains

1.question: In Amos 1:13, what is charged against the children of Ammon?
options: They put out the eyes of the elders of Gilead in a time of complete peace
They ripped up the women with child of Gilead, to enlarge their border
They burned the priests of Judah alive inside their very own sacred temple
They sold the orphans of Israel as slaves to the traders

2.question: In Amos 2:4, why is judgment pronounced against Judah?
options: They worshipped the idols of neighboring nations and forsook the temple
They despised the law of the Lord and have not kept his commandments
They made a league with the Philistines against their own people
They set up strange altars upon the sacred mountains of Judah

2.title: Tall as the cedars
2.text: Verse 9 recalls how the Lord destroyed the Amorite before Israel — 'whose height was like the height of the cedars, and he was strong as the oaks' — a reminder that Israel's land was a gift, not an achievement.

2.question: According to Amos 2:11, whom did the Lord raise up from among Israel's sons and young men?
options: Kings and judges
Prophets and Nazarites
Priests and scribes
Warriors and captains

3.question: In Amos 3:3, what rhetorical question opens the chain of images?
options: Can two walk together, except they be agreed?
Shall the horses run upon the rock without stumbling on the way?
Can the river return to its springs without any man seeing it?
Shall the shepherd sleep while the wolf devours the flock?

3.title: God reveals his secret
3.text: Amos 3:7 — 'the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets' — is one of the Bible's clearest statements that God works through prophets.

3.template: For they know not to do {0}

3.question: According to Amos 3:15, which houses will the Lord smite?
options: The walls of Samaria together with the fortified towers of Bethel
The winter house with the summer house, and the houses of ivory
The altars of Gilgal along with the palaces of Damascus
The royal storehouses and the temples of the strange gods

4.template: Hear this word, ye {0} of Bashan

4.question: In Amos 4:4, to which two places does the Lord ironically say 'come and transgress'?
options: Zion and Jerusalem
Beth-el and Gilgal
Samaria and Damascus
Tyre and Sidon

4.question: What refrain closes each of the Lord's chastisements in Amos 4?
options: Seek ye me always and ye shall find rest
Yet have ye not returned unto me
Return unto me and ye shall be blessed
Keep my commandments and ye shall live

4.question: How does Amos 4:13 describe the God of hosts?
options: He that formeth the mountains, and createth the wind, and declareth unto man what is his thought
He that reigns only over the high mountains of Samaria and completely ignores the distant nations
He that dwells only in the highest heavens and never comes down to speak directly with the men of the earth
He that punishes only the proud kings and always spares the common and humble people

5.question: In Amos 5:4, what does the Lord tell the house of Israel?
options: Seek ye me, and ye shall live
Weep and mourn bitterly before my presence
Return now unto Bethel and worship there
Keep silence in my temple

5.title: The maker of the constellations
5.text: Amos 5:8 names the Lord as the one who 'maketh the seven stars and Orion' — pointing Israel from their idols to the God who set the very constellations in the sky.

5.question: In Amos 5:8, what does the Lord do with the waters of the sea?
options: He calls for them and pours them out upon the face of the earth
He gathers them together into one place so that the dry land appears
He divides them in half so that the people may cross over in safety
He turns them to blood because of the sin of the people

5.question: According to Amos 5:14, what are the people to seek that they may live?
options: Good, and not evil
Wealth and honor
Kings and armies
Signs and wonders

5.template: Hate the evil, and love the good, and establish {0} in the gate

5.question: According to Amos 5:18-20, what will the day of the Lord be for those who desire it?
options: Light and gladness
Darkness, and not light
Rest and feasting
Victory over the nations

5.question: In Amos 5:24, what does the Lord say should run down as waters?
options: Judgment
Blood
Oil
Wine

6.title: Beds of ivory
6.text: Verse 4 pictures the elite lying 'upon beds of ivory' and eating lambs and calves — archaeology at Samaria has uncovered ivory inlays that match this indictment of luxury.

6.question: In Amos 6:6, why is woe pronounced on those who drink wine in bowls?
options: They are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph
They worship the idols of Bashan instead of the Lord
They refuse to hear the words of the prophets
They sell the poor for a pair of shoes

6.template: for ye have turned judgment into {0}

6.question: According to Amos 6:14, what will the Lord raise up against the house of Israel?
options: A drought that shall consume the rivers and the springs
A nation to afflict them from the entering in of Hemath
An earthquake that shall shake the foundations of the cities
A cloud of locusts over all the land

7.title: The prophet who argued back
7.text: In chapter 7 Amos does not merely deliver judgment — he intercedes. Twice he pleads 'O Lord God, forgive... by whom shall Jacob arise? for he is small,' and twice the Lord relents.

7.question: In the first two visions of Amos 7, what does Amos plead about Jacob?
options: That Jacob will be utterly destroyed because of sin
By whom shall Jacob arise? for he is small
That the Lord will show no mercy to Jacob
That Jacob will turn to another god

7.question: In the third vision, what does the Lord hold in his hand upon the wall (Amos 7:7)?
options: A weighing scale
A plumbline
A shepherd's staff
A wax seal

7.question: How does the priest Amaziah try to silence Amos (Amos 7:12-13)?
options: By ordering the king's soldiers to seize him at once and accuse him of treason
By telling him to flee to Judah and prophesy not at Beth-el, the king's chapel
By threatening him with death if he continued to prophesy against King Jeroboam
By forbidding him to speak before the people anywhere in Israel

8.question: In Amos 8:5, how do the greedy merchants cheat the poor?
options: Making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances
Mixing chaff together with the wheat and selling it as pure grain to the needy
Demanding forced labor from the poor in exchange for a small handful of grain
Hiding the good wheat and selling only the inferior grade of grain

8.question: According to Amos 8:10, what will the Lord turn the people's feasts into?
options: Silence
Mourning
Rejoicing
Fasting

8.question: In Amos 8:11, what kind of famine does the Lord promise to send?
options: A famine of hearing the sacred temple songs
A famine of hearing the words of the Lord
A famine of great visions and prophetic dreams
A famine of wheat, new wine, and oil

9.question: In Amos 9:2-3, what does the Lord say about escaping his judgment?
options: No hiding place — not hell, heaven, Carmel, nor the bottom of the sea — will deliver them
Only those who take refuge in the temple at Jerusalem will find protection from the judgment
Those who repent before the day of the Lord will be spared from total destruction and ruin
Only the priests of Beth-el will be spared from the coming final judgment

9.title: No place to hide
9.text: The fifth and final vision opens with the Lord standing upon the altar. Its poetry — 'though they climb up to heaven, thence will I bring them down' — echoes the reach later sung in Psalm 139.

9.question: According to Amos 9:8, what does the Lord promise about the house of Jacob?
options: He will utterly destroy it
He will not utterly destroy it
He will scatter it forever
He will forget it

9.question: How does the book of Amos close, in Amos 9:14-15?
options: With the utter and complete destruction of all the tribes of Israel because of idolatry
With a promise to bring again the captivity of Israel and plant them upon their land
With a call for Israel to turn and abandon the idols of the many neighboring nations
With the announcement of yet another period of captivity for Israel
